items.markdown:
A sudden drop in water pressure is usually caused by a **partially closed main valve, a broken pressure regulator, or a hidden leak**.[](https://www.facebook.com/plumbingpals/videos/do-you-have-low-water-pressurehere-are-the-top-5-reasons-it-happens-and-what-cau/844552675069604/) [[1]](https://www.facebook.com/plumbingpals/videos/do-you-have-low-water-pressurehere-are-the-top-5-reasons-it-happens-and-what-cau/844552675069604/)

Local and Municipal Issues

- **City work or main breaks:** Your local water provider might be doing repair work or experiencing an unexpected main break in your neighborhood.
- **Peak usage times:** High demand in your area during morning or evening hours can cause a temporary drop.[](https://www.facebook.com/plumbingpals/videos/do-you-have-low-water-pressurehere-are-the-top-5-reasons-it-happens-and-what-cau/844552675069604/) 

Home Valve and Regulator Problems

- **Main shutoff valve:** The main water valve to your home might have been bumped or accidentally turned to a partially closed position.
- **Pressure-reducing valve (PRV):** If your home has a PRV and it fails, it can restrict water flow and cause low pressure everywhere.[](https://www.berico.com/why-is-my-water-pressure-suddenly-low-throughout-the-house/) [[1]](https://www.berico.com/why-is-my-water-pressure-suddenly-low-throughout-the-house/)

Leaks and Blockages

- **Hidden water leaks:** A major leak in your walls or underground main line can divert water away from your faucets.
- **Clogged fixtures:** If only one sink or shower is affected, mineral buildup in the faucet aerator or showerhead is likely the culprit.
- **Hot water only:** If only hot water has low pressure, sediment buildup in your water heater may be blocking the output pipe.[](https://www.berico.com/why-is-my-water-pressure-suddenly-low-throughout-the-house/) [[1]](https://www.parkerandsons.com/blog/why-is-my-shower-pressure-suddenly-low)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bqwStAIZ4es&t=66)

For tips on how to measure your home's water pressure with a test gauge to see if it falls below the normal range:![Related video thumbnail](https://encrypted-tbn1.gstatic.com/images?q=tbn:ANd9GcTEg4ZHETqUP6NIB68zKwYLpK10HcXMrtgW-qcDSA3r-yKjrqWF)
